component.name: reveal-sdk-node-ai
component.description: Reveal SDK AI plugin for Node.js — adds AI capabilities to Reveal BI dashboards

properties.name: infragistics:scope
properties.value: AI wrapper plus the npm production graph of reveal-sdk-node resolved from the declared range >=2.3.0. The engine that reveal-sdk-node downloads in its install script is not inventoried here.

properties.name: io.revealbi.sbom.platform-resolution
properties.value: Platform independent. The package contains no OS- or architecture-specific binaries; the platform engine is downloaded by the reveal-sdk-node install script, which was not run.

properties.name: io.revealbi.sbom.inventory-scope
properties.value: npm production dependencies of reveal-sdk-node-ai@1.3.2 from a clean install on 2026-11-26 (npm 11.4.2, --omit=dev, --ignore-scripts; dependency edges from package-lock.json). The declared range reveal-sdk-node >=2.3.0 resolved to 2.3.2; a later install can select different versions. Plus the .NET assemblies bundled under native/, identified as NuGet packages. Excluded: the engine downloaded by the reveal-sdk-node install script, host-provided assemblies the plugin loads from the Reveal engine, and host operating-system libraries.

properties.name: reveal:vex:assessment-scope
properties.value: Reveal AI 1.3.2 for Java (io.revealbi:reveal-sdk-ai) and Node (reveal-sdk-node-ai): the AI wrapper, the bundled .NET AI assemblies, the Maven runtime graph of reveal-sdk-servlet 2.3.0 and the npm production graph of reveal-sdk-node 2.3.2. The OS-selected Reveal engine, host-provided .NET assemblies, separately downloaded Chromium and host OS libraries are outside scan coverage.

properties.name: reveal:vex:assessment-method
properties.value: Resolved the published POM and npm package graphs and identified the bundled .NET assemblies by SHA-256 match against published NuGet packages. OSV-Scanner matched inventoried packages against complete local NuGet/npm/Maven databases with network access and transitive resolution disabled. Decisions use advisory prerequisites and released bytecode (javap) and JavaScript inspection; unresolved configuration or call-path exposure remains in_triage.

properties.name: infragistics:install-script
properties.value: Downloads the platform engine at install time; not run during this assessment.

properties.name: infragistics:required-platform-sbom
properties.value: Reveal Server SDK Node 2.3.2 SBOM (win-x64 or linux-x64) for the engine

vulnerabilities.description: basic-ftp: Uncaught TypeError in MLSD directory-listing parser via __proto__ fact name causes DoS in Client.list()
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Review HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY settings and avoid FTP-backed PAC URLs. Patched basic-ftp releases are 6.x; pick them up through an upstream get-uri update or, after testing, an application-level npm override.

analysis.detail: basic-ftp is reachable through get-uri -> pac-proxy-agent -> proxy-agent -> @puppeteer/browsers in reveal-sdk-node 2.3.2. Reveal downloads a fixed HTTPS browser build, but the downloader constructs ProxyAgent and honors proxy environment variables, including pac+ftp, and get-uri can invoke Client.access, Client.list and Client.downloadTo. The default configuration does not require FTP, but deployment proxy configuration is not controlled by the release artifact. Re-checked for AI 1.3.2: the install resolved reveal-sdk-node 2.3.2 with a tarball SHA-256 identical to the 2.3.2 assessment, and identical versions and integrity for this chain. reveal-sdk-node-ai adds no caller (its index.js requires only fs and path). Fixed basic-ftp releases are 6.x only, and get-uri 6.0.5 requires basic-ftp ^5.0.2.

vulnerabilities.description: extract-zip allows arbitrary file writes through symlink archive entries

analysis.detail: reveal-sdk-node 2.3.2 lib/exporter/PuppeteerUtils.js selects the fixed Chrome Headless Shell build 132.0.6834.110 from the upstream browser distribution and a fixed per-user cache directory. Reveal exposes no archive, archive URL or extraction path input to this call; the attack requires substituting a malicious archive for that trusted distribution. Re-checked for AI 1.3.2: reveal-sdk-node 2.3.2 is byte-identical to the assessed tarball, and @puppeteer/browsers 2.13.2 and extract-zip 2.0.1 have identical integrity. reveal-sdk-node-ai does no archive handling. Supply-chain compromise or a locally tampered cache is outside this assessment; reassess if custom archive sources are introduced.

vulnerabilities.description: Zod can exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections

analysis.detail: Zod is introduced through chromium-bidi. reveal-sdk-node 2.3.2 lib/reveal.js calls puppeteer.launch({ executablePath, args }) without a protocol option, so puppeteer-core creates a CDP browser and the WebDriver BiDi schema-validation path is not used. Re-checked for AI 1.3.2: reveal-sdk-node 2.3.2 is byte-identical to the assessed tarball, and puppeteer-core 24.43.1, chromium-bidi 14.0.0 and zod 3.25.76 have identical integrity. reveal-sdk-node-ai does not use zod or Puppeteer. Reassess custom BiDi integration.
